fix(evidence): bind the watcher map's provenance to git

The map's §0-integrity block held three commit SHAs compared only to
hardcoded copies of themselves in the verifier, so the revisions did not
have to exist, be reachable, or contain anything; the six W13-W17/W23
`independentAudit` strings had the same shape, and "independent" named no
second party. Each claim is now asked of git: the published merge's exact
ordered parent list, ancestry to HEAD, byte-exact historical artifact
digests, and the pre-publication base tree; each review record binds the
revision its reviewed paths last changed at, with the summary treated as
prose and never as evidence. An optional secondPartyAudit slot is
validated structurally and is absent everywhere today. W25/W26 never
carried the field, so the manifest cites their runner-measured counts
instead. A behavioural self-test drives the real gate against 26 seeded
provenance and review-record defects with 4 accepted controls, and both
workflows that run the gate now fetch full history.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(onchain): close C49 with the four prescribed value/fee/mint selectors

C49 (issue #540) contracted closure to add exactly four prescribed Aiken
selectors to `midgard/validation_machine_v1.test`, which its focused command
already cites. Six existed and passed; the focused command exited 1 at 6/6.
This adds the four missing ones, taking the focused command to 10/10.

`parameterized_min_fee_boundary_matches_target_snapshot` instantiates the
canonical parameterized minimum-fee rule -- `body.fee >= min_fee_a *
canonical_tx_size + min_fee_b`, evaluated by `static_rules_rejection` over
`native_tx_canonical_size_v1` -- at the C70 target snapshot (minFeeA 44,
minFeeB 155_381, from `PREPROD_EPOCH_303_BOUNDARY_PARAMETERS_V1`). It pins the
two adjacent transactions at the boundary: the fee exactly at the floor
advances to InputSets, one lovelace below is an exact `E_MIN_FEE` rejection,
and neither disposition is provable against the other's transaction. The two
differ in exactly one lovelace of `body.fee`, and the fee's own CBOR width
enters the canonical size, so the test also pins the fixed point.

`parameterized_min_ada_boundary_matches_target_snapshot` pins the minimum-Ada
floor at the target snapshot `coinsPerUtxoByte = 4_310`. The row had no
min-Ada rule anywhere in `validation-machine-v1.ak`, so this adds the canonical
parameterized formula -- `min_ada_lovelace_v1` and `output_meets_min_ada_v1`,
the target-network rule verbatim over the fixed 160-byte UTxO entry overhead --
and pins it adjacently over a concrete serialized output, plus its linearity
in the serialized size. That linearity is the row's "no arbitrary sub-cap"
statement: the floor carries no Midgard margin above the target-network limit.
The floor is not yet bound to a machine rejection code on the ValueAndMint
output-descriptor scan; that wiring is the remaining min-Ada duty, and it must
consume this formula.

`parameterized_ada_and_multi_asset_conservation_matches_typescript` pins exact
signed multi-asset conservation, including the Ada rule, on the SAME numeric
vector the TypeScript twin uses in `tests/value-accounting.test.ts` over
`valuePreservationDelta`: inputs {lovelace 5, asset 2}, fee 1, mint +3, outputs
{lovelace 4, asset 5}, and the burn twin inputs {5, 5}, fee 1, mint -2, outputs
{4, 3}. Aiken reaches the same equation in two halves -- the mint step folds
the signed mint quantity into a delta already carrying inputs minus outputs
(-3, then +2), which must land on zero and drop `nonzero_asset_count`, and
stage five closes `lovelace_delta = 1` against the authenticated `body.fee =
1`. Both perturbations of that vector (outputs 5 lovelace instead of 4, a +2
mint instead of +3) are exact `E_VALUE_NOT_PRESERVED` rejections and are not
provable as advances.

`mint_and_burn_authorization_rejects_unbacked_policy` pins that a mint step may
only move an asset delta for a policy the authenticated native mint frontier
commits to. Per the post-#532 standard this is not a bare `test ... fail`: each
leg is a full one-step evaluation, the authorized policy mints and burns, and
the unbacked-policy legs differ in exactly one field of the auxiliary witness
with every other stage-four conjunct surviving the substitution. The last two
conjuncts attribute the flip directly to frontier membership.

Verification. Focused command 10/10 collected and passed under the fork
(aiken-fork v1.1.23 as MIDGARD_AIKEN_BIN); whole-module fork sweep 164/164 with
0 failures, exactly 160 + 4. `midgard/validation_machine_v1` is the aiken#1389
pathological module, so no test execution is run under stock aiken v1.1.22:
stock's leg is `aiken check --skip-tests`, green, with stock/fork agreement
carried byte-for-byte by the dual-compiler blueprint-equality guard at
integration. `verify-normalized-format.mjs` PASS on both touched modules;
`git diff --check` clean; manifest quality gate 0 defects with the self-test
green.

The C49 manifest row's `expectedNonzeroCounts` moves from the forward contract
to the measured state for the Aiken half, keeping the closure history and
recording that the four TypeScript parameter cases remain outstanding.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs(evidence): re-decide the Q1x output-5 cells per family

Output 5 was OPEN for all four families because the maximum fixture measured
that the L1 envelope is exhaustible. That measurement stands, is re-run, and
finding Q1X-F5 keeps it: what changed is that the exhaustible route is no
longer the only one.

The verifier now decides the cell per family instead of holding all four open
together, and derives the decision rather than reading it. Each adversarial axis
names the families it affects; an axis counts as settled for a family only
through a remediation block this gate has just re-derived, and only where that
block records a measurement for the family itself. `chunkedProofCarriage` is
that block: its stage margins are recomputed from its own bytes, its
depth-invariance claim is recomputed from the two depths it was measured at and
required to be zero, its direct-route comparison is recomputed from the pinned
marginal cost, and its suite must pass every lifecycle it cites. A finding that
claims remediation must name the block carrying it and must still contain the
measurement it was built on, so a remediated finding is restated and never
deleted.

Q12 and Q14 become LOCAL_PASS: their maximum now fits, and neither carries the
second adversarial axis at all. Q10 and Q11 stay OPEN on that axis alone —
spend-input preimage cardinality is still unexercised for them, and the depth
remediation says nothing about it.

Every measured number in the artifact is re-measured after the wiring: the
minimal and maximum stage bytes, the depth bound's two step-01 measurements, the
per-family ceilings and the carriage journeys. The manifest records the seam on
the Q00 shared-binding row, whose ownership it is, and the per-family selectors
and commands on the four family rows.

Refs #545

test(fault-proofs): measure chunked carriage past the direct route's ceiling

`submit-init-emulator-chunked-proof-carriage.test.ts` drives the real
prepare/submit pipeline at forced branch level 22 — past the depth at which the
redeemer-carried route exhausts the 16,384-byte envelope for every one of the
four families — end to end for zero-input and invalid-range: publication, init,
both steps and the block removal, every stage inside the 20% execution reserve.

The claim that makes it a remediation is measured rather than argued: the same
journey at branch level 32, the depth a 2^128 adversary reaches, produces a
step-01 transaction of exactly the same 13,045 bytes. Ten further forced levels
cost the step transaction nothing, where the direct route would charge
10 * 276 = 2,760.

The depth is synthesised, and `synthetic-deep-proof-v1.ts` says why: a genuinely
grinded level-22 trie costs ~2^88 digests, which is the adversary's price and
the whole content of Q1X-F5, not something a fixture can pay. The proof is a
real MPF proof of a real trie shape, verified by the library's own `verify`, and
the challenged header is made to commit exactly the root it proves, so the
step's counted-root authentication is genuine. The grinded fixture in
`submit-init-emulator-max-proof-fit.test.ts` remains the source of the cost
bound; this one measures carriage.

Two pins move and are re-pinned rather than relaxed. The maximum fixture's
per-family ceilings fall from 22/22/21/23 to 20/20/19/20 and its work floor from
2^80 to 2^72: the marginal cost per level is unchanged at 276 bytes, and only
the constant moved, because every step that can open a trie now carries the
carriage dispatch. The input-no-idx canonical-proof pin drifts 0.4% in execution
units with an unchanged 7,771-byte layout, the same signature it has drifted
under before, because the shared binding recompiled.

Refs #545

feat(fault-proofs): publish and consume MPF proof chunks off-chain

`publishProofChunksV1` splits a proof into the on-chain bound of 16 steps per
publication UTxO and pays each as an inert, Ada-only, inline-datum output at
the prover's own address. Publication needs no validator: a chunk authorises
nothing, is never mutated, and the step trusts its content rather than its
provenance.

The zero-input and invalid-range step-01 builders take those chunks and switch
carriage: the reference inputs gain them, the fee input is selected from wallet
UTxOs with them removed so the step can never spend what it references, the
chunk order is derived once from the ledger-canonical reference-input order and
then re-derived from the builder context to prove the two agree, and the
merkelized `mpf_chunked_verify` withdrawal replaces the `phas` membership one.
The proof never enters the step transaction. Every other family's builder is
wrapped in the redeemer-carried arm and is otherwise untouched.

The SDK gains the carriage sums, the publication datum and the verifier's claim,
each mirroring its aiken counterpart constructor for constructor.

Refs #545

feat(onchain): wire the four proof families onto chunked MPF carriage

The four foundational families opened the challenged block's committed roots by
carrying the MPF proof in the step transaction. That route pays a measured 276
complete-signed-transaction bytes per forced branch level, so an adversary
grinding sibling keys censors the honest prover once the 16,384-byte envelope
runs out (finding Q1X-F5).

`midgard/fraud_proofs/chunked_inclusion_v1` is the one seam through which every
family reaches the published-chunk mechanism landed for #541. A step's opening
becomes a prover-chosen carriage: `NativeTxInclusionCarriage` and
`NonMembershipCarriage` keep the redeemer-carried route byte for byte and add a
route whose proof was published beforehand and whose order the step names as
indices into `tx.reference_inputs`. `verify_native_tx_in_state_queue_node_with`
holds the codec precondition, hub identity, state-queue identity and
counted-root authentication in one place and delegates only the opening, so a
carriage cannot change what is proved — only where the proof's bytes travelled.

The walk itself is merkelized, not inlined. Compiled into every step that can
open a trie it added ~3,700 bytes of spending script, which the step
transaction carries on EITHER route: the redeemer-carried route's measured
ceiling fell from branch level 21..23 to 8..9. Remediating one route by
degrading the other is not a remediation, so `validators/mpf-chunked-verify.ak`
hosts the walk for every family exactly as `phas.ak` and `pexcludes.ak` already
host the single-transaction ones. The residual cost to the direct route is the
carriage dispatch alone: ~700 bytes, two to three forced levels, re-pinned
rather than relaxed.

`ProofChallengeDatum` gains `challenged_root_domain`, authenticated at
initialization against the domain the counted-root commitment was reproduced
under. A redeemer is not retained by the ledger, so without it a reader of a
finalized challenge could not recover which of the header's seven roots was
challenged. Owner-directed deviation from the #541 brief.

Both compilers, identical counts on every touched module: double-spend
step-01 5, step-02 3; no-input step-01 5, step-03 5, step-04 4; invalid-range
step-01 8; zero-input step-01 5; chunked_inclusion_v1 15; mpf_chunked_verify 7;
common 22; mpf_chunked_proof_v1 23; mpf_proof_v1 13; challenge 23.

docs(watcher): record the consolidated WG1 and IG3 gate review

Publish the single WG1 local-watcher-gate review the B33 scope asks
for, together with the IG3 watcher security-gate review, and a verifier
that keeps it honest.

The verifier does not decide that the watcher is locally ready; it
decides that the artifact tells the truth about what has been measured.
It rejects any WG1 condition marked PASS while a predecessor it depends
on is not measured PASS, any waiver, a gate status of PASS unless all
five predecessors and all six conditions are independently PASS, and a
W44 binding whose digests or case counts do not reproduce from the
tree. It also re-derives the W44 decomposition (17 total = 14 crash
points across 7 transitions + 1 + 1 + 1), the zero-defect invariants,
and the deeper-than-finality-within-k depth binding.

Measured result: gateStatus BLOCKED, predecessors 1/5 PASS (only W44),
WG1 conditions 0/6 PASS, IG3 security conditions 2/4 PASS (public-data
independence and defined finality/rollback hold; unprovable-gap
coverage and the maturity budget do not), 0 waivers, production
readiness false. W40-W43 have no executable surface in the index at
all, and the verifier proves that claim by resolving each named
missing path against the index rather than accepting the assertion.

Refs #509

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

test(watcher): prove the W44 crash and rollback matrix

Add the exact 17-case W44 matrix as executable evidence: 14 before/after
crash points across the 7 W32 durable lifecycle transitions (detect,
persist evidence, init, steps, proof token, removal/slashing, terminal
verification), 1 ordinary pre-finality L1 rollback, 1 rollback deeper
than the configured finality depth and within the fixed Cardano
k = 2160, and 1 configured-source inconsistency.

Crashes are injected at the real journal boundary — the durable atomic
backend's compare-and-swap — on both sides of the byte replacement, so
the post-commit case reproduces the ambiguous window where a caller
cannot tell whether its transition landed. Recovery is always a
re-invocation of the same deterministic driver against the same durable
snapshot: there is no manual-surgery step anywhere in the file. Each
case measures 0 double submits, 0 duplicate rewards, 0 lost evidence,
0 false verified states and 0 unrecoverable workflows, plus the four
IG3 security conditions (public data only, configured-source
consistency, maturity budget, enabled family), and asserts that
readiness is never true from a partially recovered state.

W32 and W33 are NOT_STARTED and their modules do not exist, so the
lifecycle sequencing is driven by an in-test driver over the real W03
durable record schema and the real W03 atomic journal boundary; the
rollback and inconsistency cases drive the real W12/W13 production
entry points with no substitution. That limit is published in the
evidence artifact rather than implied away.

Counts move coherently: crash-rollback-matrix.test.ts is a new pinned
suite at 17 and the watcher focused aggregate moves 599 -> 616 across
20 files, updated in the dependency-map declaration and currentContents,
the focused-tests verifier expectedByFile map, cardinality literal, pin
table and total, the dependency-map verifier literals, the
manifest-quality gate aggregate literal, and every watcher-gate count
claim in the task manifest.

chore(dev): refresh the Graphify graph from a HEAD snapshot even on dirty checkouts

The hook no longer refuses dirty trees: the worker snapshots HEAD with
git archive (tracked bytes only) and extracts from the snapshot, so the
published graph still corresponds to exactly one commit while the
permanent working-tree dirt (preserved unprovenanced ledger edit,
untracked GOAL_ASSIST.md) stops blocking every refresh. Post-commit
dispatch is detached behind setsid+flock with an indexed-commit stamp
that collapses rapid commit bursts; make refresh-graphify-graph runs the
same worker in the foreground. Verified on the dirty tree: 41 s,
29,255 nodes / 85,130 edges, indexed-commit stamped.
